goal: Remove #SAT/counting entirely and express SAT itself as finite-field affine matrix nonsingularity over F2.

construction.input: A 3-CNF F with clauses C_1,...,C_m on Boolean variables x_1,...,x_n, with no repeated variable inside a clause.
construction.literal_false_indicator: For a positive literal x_i use f=1+x_i; for a negative literal NOT x_i use f=x_i.
construction.clause_block: For false-indicators f1,f2,f3 define G_C=[[1,f1,0],[0,1,f2],[f3,0,1]] over GF(2).
construction.clause_determinant: det(G_C)=1+f1*f2*f3, hence on GF(2)^n it equals 1 iff the clause is satisfied and 0 iff all three literals are false.
construction.decision_identity: det M_F(a)=1 iff every clause of F is satisfied by a. Therefore F is satisfiable iff there exists a in GF(2)^n with det(M_0+sum_i a_i A_i) != 0.
construction.direction_rank: rank(A_i) equals the number of occurrences of x_i because the occurrence entries lie in pairwise disjoint clause blocks and use distinct row/column coordinates. After a standard 3-SAT-4 reduction, every direction has rank at most 4.

homogeneous_linear_space_form.construction: Introduce y0 and B(y0,x)=diag(y0, y0*M_0+sum_i x_i A_i).
homogeneous_linear_space_form.identity: B is nonsingular over GF(2) iff y0=1 and M_F(x) is nonsingular. Thus SAT is equivalent to whether the linear matrix space span{B_0,B_1,...,B_n} contains a nonsingular matrix over GF(2).
homogeneous_linear_space_form.purpose: Connect the exact decision frontier to finite-field Edmonds/max-rank machinery without replacing Boolean coefficients by a larger field.

source_alignment.source: Buss, Frandsen, Shallit, The Computational Complexity of Some Problems of Linear Algebra, JCSS 58 (1999)
source_alignment.relevance: General finite-field NONSING/MAXRANK is NP-complete; this confirms that moving to GF(2) nonsingularity does not solve SAT by itself and that any polynomial algorithm must exploit the frozen clause-block / bounded-rank-direction structure.

source_alignment.source: Tovey, A simplified NP-complete satisfiability problem, Discrete Applied Mathematics 8 (1984)
source_alignment.relevance: 3-SAT remains NP-complete when every variable appears in at most four clauses, so the frozen decision reduction can be restricted to rank(A_i)<=4 without losing universality.

source_alignment.source: Ivanyos, Karpinski, Qiao, Santha, Generalized Wong sequences and their applications to Edmonds' problems, STACS 2014 / JCSS 2015
source_alignment.relevance: Polynomial algorithms exist for special matrix-space classes such as rank-1-spanned and triangularizable spaces; v1.3 asks whether the specific clause-block rank<=4 spaces admit a stronger structural algorithm rather than invoking general finite-field NONSING.

next_target.name: E8_F2_CLAUSE_BLOCK_MAXRANK_ALGORITHM_V1_4
next_target.directive: Construct a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the frozen GF(2) block-diagonal 3-clause pencil with rank<=4 variable directions, returning a satisfying assignment exactly when a nonsingular completion exists. Do not enlarge the coefficient field, do not replace Boolean coefficients by symbolic indeterminates, and do not use exhaustive assignment enumeration.
success_obligations: works for arbitrary 3-SAT after polynomial 3-SAT-4 normalization
no hidden exponential field extension, state, bitlength, or branching

scientific_ceiling.NEW_EXACT_FRONTIER: Bounded-rank GF(2) affine nonsingularity for the explicit clause-block pencil.
